status: Provisional acoustic review, not ground-truth pitch annotations or listening/transcription labels

examples.detail: Rejected 144–145 Hz observations at 3.10–3.12 s coincide with harmonic bands and repeating waveform structure. Whole-clip raw AC, raw CC and both filtered AC settings agree near 141–146 Hz. This is strong evidence that the hybrid suppresses useful speech feedback.

examples.judgement: Supported voiced onset rejected; other events mixed
examples.detail: At 0.07–0.09 s, streaming estimates 217–221 Hz agree with raw CC and filtered AC near 220–226 Hz; the harmonic spacing supports this voiced onset. Other rejected portions near 148 Hz disagree with filtered AC at about 300–328 Hz, so the whole clip cannot be classified as correct rejections or correct pitches.

examples.judgement: Weak voiced speech likely lost completely
examples.detail: All five rejected estimates at 132–134 Hz agree with both filtered AC settings; raw CC agrees with three. Harmonic spacing near 130 Hz is visible. These were the only accepted streaming estimates in this file, so the hybrid blanks it despite corroborating voicing evidence.

examples.judgement: Supported short descending voiced segment rejected
examples.detail: The 345–358 Hz rejected onset continues a descending harmonic trajectory also tracked by raw CC and filtered AC. This is evidence of loss of genuine short voicing. Later isolated estimates around 505–526 Hz remain less certain.

examples.judgement: High excursions likely pitch errors; not all events resolved
examples.detail: The 1101–1104 Hz rejections lie well above a lower speech-related harmonic structure. Filtered AC supplies lower voiced estimates around this area and does not support a 1.1 kHz fundamental. Raw AC and raw CC can share this high-frequency selection, so their agreement alone is insufficient. Isolated 467/813 Hz events are not assigned reference pitches.

examples.judgement: Likely high-frequency tracking error, much of it still retained
examples.detail: Raw streaming estimates cluster near 1070–1080 Hz while the visible low-frequency harmonic structure and filtered AC track roughly 100–160 Hz. The hybrid rejects some short pieces but retains many long pieces of the same high track. Retention here is not preservation of correct speech pitch.

Raw AC and some raw CC observations support 87 Hz, but filtered AC with top 1200 is unvoiced and top 800 follows a higher track. The spectrogram suggests stronger speech structure around 180–200 Hz. The short transient could be a low/subharmonic error or weak irregular voicing; rejection cannot be counted as a confirmed benefit.

examples.judgement: Unresolved low estimates, high event questionable
examples.detail: The 89 Hz short events are supported by raw methods but not either filtered AC setting. The visible structure and noise do not settle their fundamental. A separate 790–799 Hz event is also rejected. No automatic correctness label is assigned.
